{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wv-class-e","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"042905b9a548bdc129e33433dc09446b3e6a6890a57e68f02e5d1f60d84d9403","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wv-class-e:lineage:10","source_registry_sha256":"2261abaab8e2b1aaff5b8a336e3bfcf845adaa75847f0210442061783d7f9afb","source_liveness_sha256":"9a1fb68777f5e9d5c4b27899084cc233b265410fee506dfe6554447a61ea026e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Permits and graduated licensing","heading":"C — Permits and graduated licensing","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Permits and graduated licensing (part one)

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
No cell phones, smart glasses, Bluetooth devices or other electronic devices are permitted in the exam room, and only the applicant taking the test may be in the room [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
Driver examiners give the vision and knowledge tests at DMV-designated locations, and once you pass the required tests the examiner approves your application for processing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
To qualify for a West Virginia driver's license you must have at least twenty-forty vision in one eye [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
A Level One graduated instruction permit requires being at least fifteen years old and having written consent from a parent or legal guardian on the DMV application form, and the holder may drive only with a licensed driver at least twenty-one years old in the right front passenger seat [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
Applicants may take the written knowledge test online as part of the license application process, but the certificate from that test is not permission to drive and the applicant must still go to a DMV location for processing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
An applicant eighteen or older who completes the application, presents the required documents and passes the vision and knowledge tests receives a regular Class E instruction permit, which allows driving only while a licensed driver twenty-one or older occupies the front seat [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
A regular instruction permit is valid for six months, and if it expires the holder must retake both the vision and knowledge tests to obtain another permit [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
A permit holder who has never been licensed at Level Two or a comparable graduated level must hold the instruction permit for at least thirty days before becoming eligible for the road skills test [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
Obtaining a Level One graduated instruction permit requires being at least fifteen, passing a vision screening and a knowledge test, and presenting parental consent on the DMV form, although a married applicant under eighteen may present a certified marriage certificate instead of parental consent [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A01
Each time you apply and test for a Level One permit you must show a certified birth certificate issued by a United States state or governmental agency responsible for vital records, together with a Social Security number issued by the Social Security Administration [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A02
A Level One permit holder may drive only between five in the morning and ten at night [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A02
A Level One permit holder may carry only two additional non-family passengers besides the supervising licensed adult driver [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A02
Two convictions at Level One result in revocation of the instruction permit for ninety days [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A02
Under the zero tolerance rule a Level One permit holder may not have any measurable amount of alcohol in the system while operating a motor vehicle, and must require every occupant to obey the safety belt law [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A02
The knowledge test fee is seven dollars and fifty cents for each attempt, and the Level One graduated permit itself also costs seven dollars and fifty cents [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A02
A Level One permit holder may not use a wireless communication device while operating a motor vehicle unless the device is being used to contact a nine one one system [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A02
A Level One permit is nonrenewable, and anyone who surrenders it for any reason must complete the examination process again, hold the permit for one hundred eighty consecutive conviction-free days, and resubmit proof of identity, Social Security number and West Virginia residency [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A02
A Level One permit is issued up to the applicant's eighteenth birthday and expires on that birthday, with a thirty-day grace period beyond it to allow time to complete the road skills examination [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A02
A Level Two intermediate license requires being between sixteen and eighteen, completing every Level One requirement, having at least one hundred eighty consecutive conviction-free days at Level One immediately before the application, and passing the road skills test [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A02
A Level Two applicant must also present a parent or guardian log certifying at least fifty hours behind the wheel including at least ten hours at night, or complete a driver education course approved by the West Virginia Department of Education, bring identity and residency documents, and not use a wireless device while driving except to contact nine one one [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A02
A Level Two holder may drive without a supervising adult between five in the morning and ten at night, but must have a supervising licensed adult twenty-one or older in the vehicle between ten at night and five in the morning [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A02
The Level Two night-driving rule does not apply when the licensee is participating in, going to or returning from lawful employment, a school-sanctioned activity, a religious activity, or an emergency that requires preventing bodily injury or the death of another person [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A03
During the first six months at Level Two the holder may not carry any non-family passenger under the age of twenty, and during the second six months may carry no more than one such passenger [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A03
Like Level One permit holders, Level Two license holders may not drive with any measurable alcohol in their system and must require every occupant to follow the seat belt law [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A03
A Level Two holder under eighteen who surrenders the intermediate license for any reason must start over with a Level One instruction permit [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A03
Each time you apply and test for the Level Two license you must show a certified birth certificate from a United States vital-records agency, provide a Social Security number, the fifty-hour driving log and all documentation required for licensing [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A03
To graduate from Level One to Level Two you must be conviction-free for six months, and each conviction restarts the six-month window from the date of that conviction [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A03
Two convictions at Level One revoke the graduated permit for ninety days, after which you must re-apply and retest for the Level One permit [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A03
To graduate from Level Two to Level Three you must be conviction-free for twelve months, and a conviction restarts the twelve-month period from that point [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A03
A Level Two holder must enroll in a driver improvement program after the first conviction, failing to enroll keeps the driver at Level Two until age eighteen, and a second moving-violation conviction revokes the driving privilege until eighteen with retesting as a first-time applicant [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A03
Drivers under eighteen may not use a wireless communication device while driving except to contact a nine one one system, and a citation for such use at Level One or Level Two restarts the conviction-free period, six months at Level One and twelve months at Level Two [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A04
Once eligible for a Level Three license the driver may choose to apply for it or to keep the Level Two license and its restrictions until age eighteen [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A04
Level Three eligibility requires twelve months of conviction-free driving at Level Two, being at least seventeen, and completing all requirements, and the application is made in person at a DMV Regional Office or Testing Center [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A04
An applicant under eighteen transferring from another state without a graduated license that equals or exceeds West Virginia's Level Two, or from a jurisdiction with no graduated program, must take the road skills test and knowledge examination as if never licensed [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F35 | anchor: A04
An under-eighteen transfer applicant who presents a current driving record from the previous jurisdiction is credited with the time the previous license was held toward the required Level One period, and that record becomes part of the West Virginia driving record [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F36 | anchor: A04
The DMV may impose license restrictions for safe operation, shown by a number or letter code in the restrictions field on the front of the license with the explanation on the back, and driving in violation of a restriction is a serious offense that can bring suspension or revocation [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F37 | anchor: A04
Listed license restrictions include artificial limbs, corrective lenses, automatic transmission, mechanical signals, hand controls, outside mirrors, motor-driven cycle, daylight driving only, an ignition interlock, a spinner knob and a medical variance, and the DMV may impose others not listed [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F38 | anchor: A04
Under the Drive for Five program every driver's license expires in a year in which the holder's age is divisible by five, so a license is normally valid for five years [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F39 | anchor: A04
To phase a driver into the five-year cycle the initial license may be issued for three to seven years depending on age at renewal, so a driver who will be thirty-four in the expiry year receives a six-year license that expires at age forty [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F40 | anchor: A05
Driver's licenses issued after the first of January two thousand one expire on the holder's birthday rather than at the end of the month, and a license expiring on the eighteenth or twenty-first birthday carries a thirty-day grace period to obtain the correctly colored license [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F41 | anchor: A05
Renewal fees are five dollars for each year until the holder's age is next divisible by five, so a driver renewing at twenty-one receives a license expiring on the twenty-fifth birthday and pays twenty dollars [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F42 | anchor: A05
Young men aged fifteen to twenty-six may register with the United States Selective Service when applying for a license, permit or photo identification card by checking a box on the back of the application [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F43 | anchor: A05
An applicant who is diabetic, deaf or hard of hearing may have that designation placed on the license or identification card by indicating it on the back of the application form turned in at application [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F44 | anchor: A05
Checking the organ donor box on the back of the application sends the applicant's information to a regional organ donation group for the registry, and while registry membership can be changed online at any time, changing the designation printed on the card requires a new license and any applicable fees [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F45 | anchor: A05
An honorably discharged veteran who wants the veterans designation must have status verified through discharge documents such as the DD two fourteen form, a military identification card or a current military license plate registration card, and the DMV may also confirm plate status through the vehicle system [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F46 | anchor: A05
You must carry your driver's license when driving and produce the license or instruction permit on demand to any law enforcement officer, magistrate or DMV official, a violation is a misdemeanor, but there is no conviction if the license was valid at the time of arrest and is produced in court or at the arresting officer's office [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F47 | anchor: A06
The fee table shows a Level One permit at age fifteen expiring on the eighteenth birthday plus a thirty-day grace period for a five-dollar permit fee, a Level Two license at sixteen valid until eighteen for five dollars, and a Level Three license at seventeen valid until twenty-one for two dollars and fifty cents per year or five dollars per year when first issued at eighteen [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F48 | anchor: A06
A regular instruction permit at eighteen runs six months from issuance for seven dollars and fifty cents, a Class E driver's license costs five dollars per year with a five-dollar expired fee, a Class F license costs two dollars and fifty cents per year, a duplicate license costs seven dollars and fifty cents, and every knowledge test attempt costs seven dollars and fifty cents [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F49 | anchor: A06
An additional ten dollars is required to obtain, renew or duplicate a For Federal Identification driver's license or identification card [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F50 | anchor: A06
Along with the driver's license you must keep valid proof of West Virginia liability insurance and the current registration card in the vehicle, and show them with the license when a law enforcement officer stops you for a moving violation [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]
